what_its_for: Miconazole nitrate 2% is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal skin infections. These include athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris), ringworm (tinea corporis), and yeast infections of the skin. It works by killing the fungus causing your infection.
how_to_take: This medicine is applied directly to your skin. Before applying, wash and completely dry the affected area. Apply a thin layer of the cream, spray, or powder to the infected area and the skin right around it. Gently rub it in. Wash your hands before and after applying, unless your hands are the area being treated. For athlete's foot, pay special attention to the spaces between your toes. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Apply to the affected skin area twice a day (morning and evening), or as directed by your doctor or the product label. For athlete's foot and ringworm, use for 4 weeks. For jock itch, use for 2 weeks. Do not use more than directed, as it will not help your infection heal faster and may cause more side effects.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the one you missed. Try to apply it at the same times each day to help you remember.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the product away from heat and direct sunlight. Do not freeze the cream. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in your bathroom, as heat and moisture can damage the medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, nose, or mouth. If it gets in your eyes, rinse with plenty of water right away. Avoid wearing tight, non-breathable clothing or shoes while being treated, as this can make the infection worse. Do not use other skin products on the same area unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid sharing towels, clothing, or shoes with others, as fungal infections can spread. Keep the affected area clean and dry as much as possible.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or pharmacist if: your symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks of treatment for jock itch, or after 4 weeks for athlete's foot or ringworm; your symptoms get worse; you develop a rash, severe itching, burning, swelling, or blistering that was not there before; you think the infected area is spreading; or you notice signs of a skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, or pus. Seek emergency care if you have trouble breathing or swelling of your face, lips, or throat, as this may be a rare allergic reaction.
when_it_works: You may start to feel relief from itching and discomfort within a few days of starting treatment. However, it is very important to keep using the medicine for the full recommended time, even if you feel better sooner. Stopping too early may allow the fungus to come back. Most infections fully clear up within 2 to 4 weeks with regular use.
special_populations: Children under 2 years old: Do not use without a doctor's supervision. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine, especially for vaginal yeast infections. People with diabetes or a weakened immune system: You may be more prone to fungal infections; see your doctor if the infection is severe or keeps coming back. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustments are usually needed, but check with your doctor if you have sensitive or fragile skin.
